evals.name: slop kill: gradient hero page
evals.prompt: Rewrite this HTML so it no longer looks AI-generated. Keep the same content and purpose. Output the complete rewritten HTML.
evals.expected_output: A landing page with a deliberate, non-template design: no purple-blue gradient hero, no three identical feature cards, no invented stats.
assertions: The output contains no purple-blue or violet gradient hero or gradient text
The output does not use three or more identical equal-width feature cards
The output contains no invented statistic rows (10k+, 99.9%, 24/7)
The page has a clear visual hierarchy with one primary action
The copy avoids marketing buzzwords (streamline, empower, supercharge, seamless)

evals.name: slop kill: new-slop tells
evals.prompt: Rewrite this HTML so it no longer looks AI-generated. Keep the same content and purpose. Output the complete rewritten HTML.
evals.expected_output: A page whose design is not guessable from AI anti-reference lists.
assertions: The output does not use glassmorphism (backdrop-blur) as a default surface treatment
The output does not use the identical-icon-tile-above-heading pattern
The output does not use an accent stripe as decoration
Typography shows editorial contrast: not one font at one weight for everything
The output does not use a template hero (centered headline, 2-line subtitle, primary+ghost buttons, 100vh)

evals.name: slop kill: copy voice
evals.prompt: Rewrite only the copy of this page so it reads like a human wrote it, not an LLM. Output the revised copy with the section headings.
evals.expected_output: Copy with a specific voice and concrete claims.
assertions: The copy contains no em-dash saturation (no more than 1 per 500 characters)
The copy contains no aphoristic manufactured-contrast lines (Not a X. A Y.)
The copy avoids three-word marketing triads and 'say goodbye to X' constructions
Every claim is specific enough to be fact-checked

evals.name: build from brief: dashboard
evals.prompt: Build a single-page HTML/CSS dashboard for 'Roastline', a coffee roastery's production tool, used by ops managers to track batch yields and roast profiles. Mode: Operate. Follow the skill document if one is attached.
evals.expected_output: A functional-feeling dashboard that fits the brief.
assertions: The output is recognizably a coffee-roastery production dashboard (batch, roast, yield vocabulary)
The layout supports task completion: primary actions and data are scannable, not decorative
The output does not use the generic tech hue (#6366F1 indigo) or a blue-violet gradient
The design does not use three identical equal-weight cards for the main content
The color palette is not guessable from the product category alone

evals.name: build from brief: landing
evals.prompt: Build a landing page for 'Roastline', a coffee roastery selling subscription beans. Audience: home brewers who care about origin and freshness. Mode: Persuade. Follow the skill document if one is attached.
evals.expected_output: A persuasive landing page with a point of view.
assertions: The page has a clear persuasion structure: one hook, one primary action, proof that supports the claim
The design has a distinctive character beyond Tailwind defaults (not Inter-everything, not a template hero)
No invented stats or unverifiable claims
The output does not use an emoji as an icon
Typography has hierarchy: display, subhead, and body are visually distinct

evals.name: redesign: make it bolder
evals.prompt: Redesign this page to be bolder and more confident. Keep the content. Output the complete HTML.
evals.expected_output: The same content with a stronger, more assertive design character.
assertions: The redesign has a clearly stronger visual character than the input (bigger type, stronger contrast, more deliberate color)
Accessibility is not broken: text/background contrast remains sufficient
The redesign does not merely add gradient text or a purple-blue palette
The redesign does not increase the number of equally-weighted elements

evals.name: audit report: two axes
evals.prompt: The brief for this page: a persuasive landing page for 'Roastline', a coffee subscription for home brewers who care about origin and freshness. Audit the page against that brief AND against design standards. Produce a structured report. Follow the skill document if one is attached.
evals.expected_output: A two-axis audit report: a Standards axis and a Spec axis, reported separately.
assertions: The report has two separate axes: a Standards axis (conformance: layout, a11y, hierarchy, tells) and a Spec axis (fidelity to the coffee-subscription brief)
The two axes are reported separately and are not merged or reranked into one score
The Spec axis quotes the brief and identifies missing, partial, or scope-creep requirements
The Standards axis uses severity levels consistently and names the element and fix for each finding
No finding is invented or unsupported by the input HTML

evals.name: audit report: honesty
evals.prompt: No brief exists for this page. Audit it for design problems. The page has no images and no forms. Produce a structured report. Follow the skill document if one is attached.
evals.expected_output: An audit that stays truthful about what is and is not in the page.
assertions: The report states 'no spec available' for the Spec axis instead of inventing a brief
The report does not claim missing alt text or missing form labels exist when there are no images or forms
The report flags real issues present in the HTML (layout, hierarchy, color)
Every fix suggestion is verifiable against the input

evals.name: a11y fix: contrast and targets
evals.prompt: Fix the accessibility problems in this HTML: contrast, touch targets, and text sizing. Output the complete corrected HTML.
evals.expected_output: The page with WCAG-conformant contrast and touch targets, visually unchanged in intent.
assertions: Text on colored backgrounds meets WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large)
Interactive elements have at least 44x44px touch targets
The fix did not change the page's content or design intent
No new layout breakage was introduced

evals.name: a11y fix: semantics
evals.prompt: Fix the semantic accessibility problems in this HTML: landmarks, heading order, focus. Output the complete corrected HTML.
evals.expected_output: The page with correct landmarks, a single h1, ordered headings, and visible focus states.
assertions: The page has proper landmark elements (header, main, footer or equivalent)
There is exactly one h1 and heading levels do not skip
Interactive elements have visible focus states
The fix did not change the visual design

evals.name: deslop: targeted fix
evals.prompt: This page has AI-slop tells. Identify each tell you find and fix it with a positive alternative. Output the complete rewritten HTML plus a one-line note per fix.
evals.expected_output: A page with each tell replaced by a deliberate alternative, documented.
assertions: Each identified tell was replaced, not just removed: the replacement has an intentional rationale
The fixes do not introduce a different recognizable AI tell
The page keeps its content and purpose
The notes are specific enough that a reviewer can verify each fix

evals.name: shape: grill before building
evals.prompt: The user says: 'build me a landing page for my new product'. You may ask up to 3 questions before building. Follow the skill document if one is attached.
evals.expected_output: Frontier-round grilling: the questions whose answers are needed now, each with a recommended answer, and no code written.
assertions: Every question carries a recommended answer (not an open menu)
Questions are asked in rounds on the frontier: no question depends on an answer the same round didn't settle, and none asks for a fact the agent could look up itself
Questions target register, mode, audience, and success criteria, not trivia
The response does not assume answers: it does not silently pick a register, palette, or layout for the user
No code was written before the brief is confirmed
